# Allowlist for skills_validation_test.go.
#
# Format (one entry per line):
#   <skill rel path under skills/>|<exact claim text>|<justification>
#
# A claim is either a command reference ("forge <chain>") or a path
# reference exactly as the validator reports it. Use skill path "*" to
# allowlist a claim across every skill. Every entry REQUIRES a
# justification — unexplained entries fail the test. Entries whose claim
# no longer appears in the named skill fail TestSkillsAllowlistEntriesStillNeeded.

*|forge will not overwrite this file|canonical "yours" ownership banner text quoted in code blocks — prose, not a forge subcommand
forge/deploy/SKILL.md|forge env deploy --env|Counter-example, not a claim: the sentence exists to tell the reader the environment is a POSITIONAL arg — "`forge env deploy dev`, not `forge env deploy --env dev`". Deleting the wrong spelling would delete the correction.
forge/auth/dev-loop/SKILL.md|.forge/idp/pat.txt|Runtime artifact, not a scaffolded file: the dev IdP WRITES this path on its first boot (forge sets it as ZITADEL_FIRSTINSTANCE_PATPATH, and .gitignore excludes .forge/*). The skill must name it because forge reads the credential from there when it registers the browser application, and a developer debugging a failed bring-up needs to know where to look.
forge/auth/dev-loop/SKILL.md|.forge/hostinfra/idp/zitadel.log|Runtime artifact, not a scaffolded file: the host-process dev IdP writes its stdout/stderr there (internal/hostinfra/zitadel.go), and it is the first thing to read when the IdP never comes up. .gitignore excludes .forge/*.
*|forge secret set dev|Positional-arg artifact, not a stale command: the real form is `forge secret set <env> <KEY>` (ExactArgs(2)). The validator's chain regex only captures LOWERCASE tokens, so it sees `secret set dev` and asks cobra to validate one positional against ExactArgs(2), which correctly fails. The uppercase KEY that makes the invocation valid is invisible to the regex.
